title: Kung Fu Chaos
subtitle: A brawl takes place on a film set

body: Kung Fu Chaos is Just Add Monsters' Xbox party fighting game, released in North America on 25 February 2003. Its stages are scenes in an imaginary martial-arts film, with a director commenting on the action as the cast attempts to survive it. Up to four players fight through sets that can be as important as the opponents occupying them. The film premise gives the game permission to change circumstances rapidly, replacing a stable arena with moving scenery, timed dangers and comic interruptions that demand attention beyond the person immediately being punched.

Quick and heavy attacks, throws, blocks and counters provide the basic fighting vocabulary. After defeating an enemy, a player can taunt to build towards a powerful special attack. Performing the taunt leaves the character briefly vulnerable, creating an opportunity for someone else to interrupt or steal the moment. The reward therefore depends on choosing when the scene is safe enough to celebrate. Campaign progress also requires a sufficient performance rating, connecting survival and fighting to the director's evaluation of the scene rather than merely reaching its final few seconds.

Just Add Monsters began with a small, self-funded prototype before obtaining the support needed to finish the game. Reviews appreciated the tone and inventive stages while questioning the depth of the fighting; some also criticised its racial stereotypes. Sales disappointed, and a planned sequel was cancelled. The studio later became Ninja Theory and developed Heavenly Sword. Kung Fu Chaos established an early interest in strongly directed visual presentation, using the setting of a chaotic film shoot to make the level itself an active participant in the multiplayer brawl.
